title: Where to start
instr: Pick the route that matches why you’re here.

routes.label: New to Oath & Action
routes.lede: Start here to learn what Oath & Action is and how to read what we publish.

steps.text: Find out what Oath & Action does and what our four pillars, Explain, Track, Connect and Act, each stand for.
Check the label above a headline to see what kind of piece you are reading.
When we take a side on a measure, the piece opens with the label “Our position” and gives the strongest case against it.
The evidence grade beside a claim, from documented to hypothesis, tells you how sure that claim is.
Read the word Illustrative as our sign that the item beside it is invented.
See how a tracker follows a bill through six numbered steps, from filing to the governor’s or president’s desk.
Every piece ends on one step you can take, with its date and the way to take it.

routes.label: Designing a piece
routes.lede: Use this route when you design anything we publish, on screen or in print.

steps.text: Choose the lockup, our name and marks set in one fixed arrangement, by the width you have and the surface it sits on.
Start on Newsprint, our warm off-white page, and set text only on color pairs with enough contrast.
Spend red on one job in each view, such as the step a reader can take now.
Take every type size from the type scale, and set nothing on screen under 13 px.
Space the page with the 8 px spacing scale, on the column grid for its width.
See the identity at true size on four of our pieces, from the site’s masthead to a letterhead.
Chapters 20 to 25, which come later, will show each kind of piece in full, from a web page to a printed report.

routes.label: Building with code
routes.lede: When you build in code, take every color, size, space and speed from our tokens, the named values in two files.

steps.text: Download tokens.css and tokens.json, which hold the same tokens under one version number.
Link tokens.css before your own styles, then give the body its margin and type.
Choose each token in five steps, starting from the surface it sits on.
Let the page follow the reader’s light or dark setting through one attribute on its root.
Copy each control’s code from chapter 18, where every control works by keyboard and screen reader.
Give each of the ten states, from hover to error, words or a shape as well as a color.
Before you call a page finished, run the checks in chapter 19 against WCAG 2.2 at level AA, the accessibility standard we build to.
